Heading back from Koh Lanta to Bangkok the easiest and most sensible way is to get to the mainland either by van/ferry or by boat first and then proceed to the capital by plane or by bus. If you want to travel by train, your best bet is Suratthani or Chumphon, but you will need to reach either of them by bus first. If you do not want to plan your trip to Bangkok all by yourself, there are a lot of tour agencies in Ban Saladan on Koh Lanta ready to offer you package tours to Bangkok, but as prices, travel times and means of transport included into such packages vary greatly, always check the itinerary in advance to avoid any possible disappointment of spending much more in terms of money and time than you have expected (e.g. if going via Koh Phi Phi, for instance).

is probably a more convenient stop on your way to Bangkok from Koh Lanta as it is the closest to Koh Lanta large town on the firm land and can be reached not only by boat but by van+ferry as well. Vans drive through to Koh Lanta Noi which is now connected to Koh Lanta Yai by a new bridge and then take a car ferry from Koh Lanta Noi to the mainland (7 minutes; but you may need to queue for a fair amount of time, especially during high season). Shop around to find deals under THB600 per person for a van ride from Koh Lanta to Krabi airport. The distance your van has to cover is around 75 km, and it takes under two hours to get from Koh Lanta to Krabi airport.

sources.quote: To get to Bangkok from Koh Chang you need to take a ferry to the mainland first and then hop onto a van or a bus heading to the capital. There are combo deals which include pick-up at your hotel in Koh Chang, a ferry ride and a bus ride or just a ferry and a bus ride alone. You can as well take a ferry from the pier on Koh Chang (tickets cost THB80; departures every hour) all by yourself and then look for transport at the mainland pier or in Trat (to get there from any pier, take a songthaew for THB50-60). Normally, combo deals cost more or less the same as separate tickets but save you a good deal of time.

notes: Method: 12Go.asia route pages were rendered in headless Chrome (WebFetch is blocked by the 12Go WAF) on 10.10.2026. Default pages show trips for Tue 13.10.2026 (low season); pages with ?date=2026-12-15 show the high-season timetable. Each quote is verbatim rendered text; ' / ' separates consecutive text nodes on the page (e.g. a trip card: duration / from / to / operator / type). | SEASONAL (important): the direct speedboats Koh Lipe <-> Koh Lanta / Phi Phi / Phuket / Krabi(Railay-Ao Nang) / Koh Ngai / Langkawi were verified on the 15.12.2026 timetable (Bundhaya Speed Boat, Satun Pakbara Speed Boat Club). On the 13.10.2026 page Lanta->Lipe shows only Van+Ferry via the mainland (7h). go-ferry lists Lanta-Lipe and Langkawi-Lipe as 'Oct – May'. If the post should be season-proof, consider a sub-line under the Koh Lipe heading such as 'בעונה (נובמבר-אפריל):' - not added because his format rarely has it. | Koh Lanta -> Phi Phi and -> Phuket (Bundhaya, Saladan -> Ton Sai / Rassada) run on both the October and December pages. | 'קראבי' from Koh Lipe = the Bundhaya speedboat to Railay East Pier, Ao Nang (Krabi province), 5h40. From Koh Lanta 'קראבי' = shared van to Krabi Town (2h, At Lanta Vacation). | Koh Lanta -> Bangkok: no single ticket; 12Go's own guide says get to the mainland by van/ferry or boat and then fly (Krabi or Phuket airport). Mode written as 'ואן + טיסה'. | Koh Chang -> Samui / Phuket / Chiang Mai: flights leave from Trat Airport (TDX) on the mainland, so the realistic chain is ferry off the island + flight; 12Go lists Bangkok Airways flights from TDX (20 to USM on 15.12). Whether TDX-USM is non-stop was not verified - irrelevant to the mode wording. | Koh Chang -> Koh Samet: 12Go sells Van + Speedboat transfers and Ferry+Van combos; written as 'ואן + מעבורת' (the car ferry off Koh Chang is part of the van leg). | Chiang Rai -> Phuket / Krabi: 12Go shows connecting flights (Flight+Flight, self-connect). A Thai Vietjet non-stop CEI-HKT was reported for 2026 but not seen on 12Go - wording 'טיסה' is correct either way. | Chiang Rai -> Luang Prabang: 12Go's bestseller is Van+Train (11h30, via the Laos-China railway); the classic 2-day slow boat (Van+Ferry) also exists - swap to 'ואן + סירה' only if he prefers the iconic option. | Chiang Rai -> Golden Triangle: 12Go sells only private car/taxi transfers (55m-1h) - written 'רכב'. | Dropped (could not verify a sensible traveller option or slide full): Chiang Rai -> Koh Samui (12Go shows only a 22h taxi), Koh Chang -> Siem Reap, Koh Lipe -> Penang (verified Ferry+Van 8h13 but left out for space), Koh Lanta -> Koh Ngai (verified 30m speedboat in December, left out for space). | Destination emoji copies his slide exactly: 🏝️ on every row, including cities.
